body:
_Migrated from issue #1204, filed 2026-07-28._

Surfaced by #1201. With the integration suite running again, it reports `68 passed, 50 skipped, 0 errors` — but 36 of those 50 skips are the kosync tests, and they skip for a reason worth fixing rather than accepting:

| file | skipped |
|---|---|
| `tests/integration/test_kosync_edge_cases.py` | 17 |
| `tests/integration/test_progress_syncing_kosync.py` | 14 |
| `tests/integration/test_kosync_update_read_status.py` | 5 |
| `tests/docker/test_container_startup.py` | 5 |
| `tests/integration/test_ingest_checksums.py` | 2 |

All the kosync ones depend on `cwa_api_client`, which gives up here:

```python
login_response = session.post(
    f"{base_url}/login",
    data={"username": "admin", "password": "admin123"},
    allow_redirects=False, timeout=5)

if login_response.status_code not in (200, 302):
    pytest.skip("Could not authenticate with CWA container")
```

The container is up and reachable — the 19 ingest tests in the same run drive it successfully — so this is the login specifically, not availability. Reproduced locally too: `test_percentage_at_zero` spends 13.6s in fixture setup and then skips with that message.

The effect is that KOReader progress sync, kosync validation, and read-status thresholds currently have **no** integration coverage, and the suite still reports green. A skip is invisible in a way a failure is not, which is the same shape of problem as #1202 — CI saying "fine" about something it never exercised.

Worth checking whether `admin/admin123` is still right for the seeded test container, whether the login route needs a CSRF token the fixture isn't sending, or whether the fixture should hard-fail rather than skip once the container is confirmed up. A skip that is really "the harness cannot log in" should not look the same as "this test does not apply here".

Related: #1201, #1202, #1105, #953.
title: Integration: 36 kosync tests skip because cwa_api_client cannot log in
